title: Money basics
description: What money is, saving, keys and why the vault opens at 18. Four of the six lessons from the Learn page, chosen for ages 6 to 9. Interest and Bitcoin itself move to the 10 to 13 pack.

lessons.title: What money is
paragraphs: Long ago, people traded things directly: a basket of apples for a pair of shoes. That only works when both people want what the other has.
Money fixes this. It is something everyone agrees to accept, so you can sell apples today and buy shoes next week.
Good money is easy to carry, easy to split into small parts, hard to fake, and it keeps its value over time.
lessons.tryThis: Look at a coin or a note together. Who made it? Why do shops accept it?

quiz.prompt: Why do shops accept money instead of apples?
choices: Because everyone agrees to accept it
quiz.explanation: Money works because everyone agrees it counts. That agreement is what makes it useful.

lessons.title: Saving
paragraphs: Saving means keeping some money now so you can use it later. It is a choice between something small today and something bigger tomorrow.
A goal makes saving easier. Write down what you are saving for and how much it costs.
Every small amount counts. Putting a little aside many times adds up to a lot.
lessons.tryThis: Pick one thing you want. Work out how many weeks of saving it takes.

quiz.prompt: You save 2 coins every week. How many coins after 5 weeks?
quiz.explanation: 2 coins times 5 weeks is 10 coins. Small amounts add up.

lessons.title: Keys, and why you never share them
paragraphs: In Bitcoin, owning money means holding a secret key. The key signs a message that says "move these coins". Anyone who has the key can do that.

A recovery phrase is a list of 12 words that can rebuild the key. Write it on paper and keep it somewhere safe. Never type it into a website you did not choose, never send it in a message, and never show it to someone who asks for it.
If the words are lost, nobody can help you get the coins back. There is no "forgot password" button in Bitcoin.
lessons.tryThis: Ask: who in our family knows where the recovery paper is? Is that enough people, or too many?

quiz.prompt: A game on the internet asks you to type your 12 secret words to win a prize. What do you do?
choices: Close it and tell a grown-up
quiz.explanation: Nobody honest ever asks for your secret words. Close it and tell a trusted grown-up.

lessons.title: Why the vault opens at 18
paragraphs: The demo vault on this site has two locks. The parent key opens it at any time, and the child key opens it only after the 18th birthday. The rule is written inside Bitcoin itself: until the date arrives, the network refuses to accept a payment signed by the child key.

The next vault removes the parent lock. Parents, grandparents and friends can put coins in, but nobody can take them out before the child is 18. Only three guardians the family chose can act in an emergency, after a long wait, and only to send the coins to a charity for children.
Waiting is part of the lesson. It gives the savings time to grow and gives the child time to learn how to look after money before they are in charge of it.
lessons.tryThis: Look at the unlock date on your vault. How old will you be? What would you like to have learned by then?
